html.body: Date: 2025-03-07 REMARKS/ARGUMENTSReconsideration of the application in light of the foregoing amendments and following remarks/arguments is respectfully requested.Status of Action Claims 1-10 were rejected. Claims 1, 3-8, 10 are currently amended, claim 2 is canceled.Drawings were objected. Drawings are currently amended.Specification was objected. Specification is addressed but not amended.All amendments were made for clarity. No new matter is added.Upon entry of these amendments, claims 1, 3-10, drawings and specification will be pending.Drawing Obiections The drawings are objected to because the cut away "A" and "B" figures (figures 8 and 9) are incorrectly labelled.In response to drawing objections under 37 CFR1.121(d), Fig. 8 has been amended to show part "A" in figure 1, and Fig. 9 has been amended to show part "B" in figure 1.Specification Obiection Response to specification objection regarding use of "stimulating" vs."simulating", we confirm that the intended terminology is "stimulating" and "stimulate" after reviewing the paragraphs in question ([0004], [0069], and [0070]) .These terms accurately describe the function of the invention, as one of the purposes of the electric wave generator is to actively stimulate brain activity to enhance focus, alertness, and learning abilities. Specifically, the device emits high-frequency alpha waves or mid-low frequency beta waves, which are intended to stimulate the brain and create a sense of excitement in the brains of students and teachers, helping them stay alert, absorb knowledge better, stimulate creativity, and enhance learning abilities.To clarify:"Stimulating" is the correct term when describing the device's function to actively influence brain activity to promote alertness and focus. "Simulating" is not the intended term in these contexts, as the device does not merely mimic brain wave signals but rather actively stimulates them to achieve the desired cognitive effects."Simulating" is the correct term when describing the device's ability to replicate or mimic brain wave signals that correspond to natural states, such as those associated with sleep, relaxation, or heightened focus. The electric wave generator is designed to simulate various brain wave patterns that mimic human brain activity, and when paired with an intelligent Al monitoring system, it allows for precise adjustments to the intensity and duration of the waveforms according to the user's needs.We trust this clarification addresses your inquiry and provides sufficient detail regarding the intended functionality of the claimed invention. Please do not hesitate to contact us if further clarification is needed.Claim Obiections The term "withe" in line 12 of the original claim 4 was amended to read "with".The term "of protective box" in line 2 of the original claim 5 was amended to read "of the protective box". The term "a multifunctional electric wave generator" in line 1 of the original claim 10 was amended to read "the multifunctional electric wave generator".Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112 Claim 1 Regarding the term in the preamble of Claim 1, the applicant would like to clarify that the intended word is indeed "simulation", as the multifunctional electric wave generator is designed for the simulation of brain waves. The device is intended for replicating and generating specific brain wave patterns to influence brain activity in a controlled manner.As is known, there are five main types of brain waves (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, and Gamma) that are naturally produced by the human brain. These waves are associated with specific states of mind and physiological conditions. It is well-known in the field of neurophysiology that:Delta Waves (0-3 Hz): Associated with deep relaxation, recovery, and sleep.Theta Waves (3-8 Hz): Linked to drowsiness, meditation, and heightened suggestibility.Alpha Waves (8-12 Hz): Present when the brain is relaxed, closed-eyes, and in a resting state.Beta Waves (12-27 Hz): Dominant during active thinking, problem-solving, and concentration.Gamma Waves (Above 27 Hz): Involved in higher cognitive processing and information processing.As described in the specification (paragraphs [0069]-[0072]), the multifunctional electric wave generator is designed to simulate these brain waves in a controlled environment, such as a closed room. The device can detect and adapt to the user's needs (with the assistance of an Al system) to emit specific brain wave signals. For example:In an educational setting, the device can emit beta waves to help students maintain alertness and focus, reducing drowsiness and improving learning efficiency.For individuals struggling with sleep disorders, the device can emit alpha waves to create a relaxing environment, helping the brain transition into a sleep-conducive state and improving sleep quality.The device achieves this by generating electrical signals that mimic the natural brain wave patterns, effectively influencing the brain's state without directly interfering with its physiological processes. This simulation is designed to create an environment where the brain can more easily adopt the desired state, whether it be alertness, relaxation, or sleep.We trust this clarification addresses your inquiry and provides sufficient detail regarding the intended functionality of the claimed invention. Please do not hesitate to contact us if further clarification is needed.Claim 1-10 In the Office Action, the Examiner rejected Claims 1-10 under 35 U.S.C.112(b) or 35 U.S.C.112 (pre-AIA) , as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AlA U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention. It is believed that the amendments incorporated into the Claims hereby now obviate the Examiner's formal concerns, including those set forth under 35 U.S.C.112, second paragraph.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 Claim 1 is rejected under 35 U.S.C.103 as being unpatentable over lves (US4806881A) in view of Sanus ("CFR2115, CFR2127, CFR2136, CFR2144 Instruction Manual", 2014) and Al-Samman ("Comparative Study of Indoor Propagation Model Below and Above 6 GHz for 5G Wireless Networks", 2019).Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C.103 as being unpatentable over lves (US4806881A), Sanus ("CFR2115, CFR2127, CFR2136, CFR2144 Instruction Manual", 2014) and Al-Samman ("Comparative Study of Indoor Propagation Model Below and Above 6 GHz for 5G Wireless Networks", 2019), in view of Leger ("How to Use a Function Generator", 2013).In response, claim 1 has been amended to add the limitations of claim 2, and claim 2 has been canceled. Therefore, amended claim 1 is unobvious and patentable under 35 U.S.C.103 over lves (US4806881A) in view of Sanus ("CFR2115, CFR2127, CFR2136, CFR2144 Instruction Manual", 2014) and Al-Samman ("Comparative Study of Indoor Propagation Model Below and Above 6 GHz for 5G Wireless Networks", 2019). Claim 10 depends on amended claim 1 is unobvious and patentable under 35 U.S.C.103 over lves (US4806881A), Sanus ("CFR2115, CFR2127, CFR2136, CFR2144 Instruction Manual", 2014) and Al-Samman ("Comparative Study of Indoor Propagation Model Below and Above 6 GHz for 5G Wireless Networks", 2019), in view of Leger ("How to Use a Function Generator", 2013).CONCLUSIONBased on the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection of the claims and allowance of this application.Applicant invites the Examiner to call the undersigned if clarification is needed on any of this response, or if the Examiner believes a telephonic interview would expedite the prosecution of the subject application to completion.Respectfully submitted, /Qiangian Wu/ Qiangian Wu Registration No. 78599 Dated: 03/07/2025
